jobs.title: Senior Director, Strategy Risk Business Operations and Shared Services
jobs.description:
Job Description

What is the Opportunity?

As the Senior Director, Strategy Risk Business Operations and Shared Services you will lead a high-performing team of directors, senior managers, and managers to drive strategic, operational, and financial excellence within RBC’s Commercial & Payment Technology (CPT) portfolio. This critical leadership role is accountable for Financial Management, Project Portfolio Planning, Vendor Management, Risk & Compliance, and Strategic Planning, ensuring alignment with enterprise priorities and delivering exceptional business outcomes. You will champion employee engagement, change management, and innovation (e.g., AI adoption) while maintaining rigorous governance and operational excellence.

What You'll Do

Leadership & Strategy

Lead the Planning, Risk & Governance functions, overseeing financial management, project portfolio planning, and strategic alignment with RBC’s Commercial Banking and T&O objectives.
Develop and execute CPT’s 5-year strategic plan, leveraging internal/external research and partnering with business executives to drive disciplined project management.
Champion enterprise initiatives (e.g., AI/AIDLC) and change management within CPT, ensuring successful adoption and engagement.
Foster exceptional employee engagement through targeted strategies and communication plans in partnership with Enterprise Communications.

Risk & Governance

Ensure adherence to Risk & Governance policies, standards, and control points (e.g., audits, access reviews, compliance attestations).
Lead T&O and RBC-initiated Risk & Governance campaigns, collaborating with Risk, GS, and business partners.
Oversee Business Continuity Management (BCM), including plan approvals, testing, and strategy.
Monitor Key Risk Indicators (KRIs) and escalate issues, ensuring alignment with first-line defense (Internal/External Audit).

Vendor Management

Lead the expansion of Vendor Management, optimizing on-shore/off-shore resources and negotiating multi-million-dollar contracts.
Drive cost savings, efficiencies, and service standards across vendor relationships, ensuring alignment with financial and operational targets.

Financial Management & Reporting

Define and execute the Financial Plan for application maintenance, development, and Risk & Governance efforts.
Provide timely, actionable financial reporting (budgets, forecasts, metrics) to the Senior Leadership Team (SLT) and stakeholders.
Manage IT Development, Maintenance, and Financial budgets, ensuring alignment with annual and 5-year plans.
Oversee project accruals, cost accounting, and vendor invoice management to meet overhead and recovery targets.

Operational Excellence & Performance

Monitor performance metrics, scorecards, and dashboards, driving process improvements and benchmarking.
Lead Program/Project onboarding/closure, ensuring accurate financial tracking in systems (e.g., Planview, MIS).
Leverage AI and automation for reporting and project delivery efficiencies.

People Leadership

Build and mentor a high-performing team, aligning individual goals with RBC’s Leadership Model.
Drive diversity, reward & recognition, and career development initiatives.
Instill a culture of change readiness and empowerment across CPT.

What You Need To Succeed

Must Have:

15+ years of leadership experience in Technology, Financial Services, or Operations, with expertise in Risk, Governance, and Vendor Management.
Proven track record in strategic planning, financial management, and large-scale project delivery.
Strong understanding of AI, Agile/SDLC methodologies, and regulatory compliance.
Exceptional negotiation, stakeholder management, and communication skills.
Bachelor’s degree in Business, Finance, or related field; MBA or advanced certification preferred.

Nice to Have:

Payments industry experience

What’s in it for you?

We thrive on the challenge to be our best, progressive thinking to keep growing, and working together to deliver trusted advice to help our clients thrive and communities prosper. We care about each other, reaching our potential, making a difference to our communities, and achieving success that is mutual.

A comprehensive Total Rewards Program including bonuses and flexible benefits, competitive compensation, commissions, and stock where applicable
Leaders who support your development through coaching and managing opportunities
Ability to make a difference and lasting impact
Work in a dynamic, collaborative, progressive, and high-performing team
Opportunities to do challenging work
Opportunities to take on progressively greater accountabilities
Opportunities to building close relationships with clients

The Alcohol and Gaming Commission of Ontario (AGCO)
is an agency where innovation thrives, ideas flourish, and passion drives us to new heights of excellence. Reporting to the Ministry of the Attorney General, the AGCO is responsible for regulating Ontario’s vibrant alcohol, gaming, horse racing, and private retail cannabis sectors in accordance with the principles of honesty and integrity, and in the public interest.

The Alcohol and Gaming Commission of Ontario (AGCO) is seeking a strategic, collaborative and forward-thinking leader to serve as Director, People and Culture Strategy. Reporting to the Chief Human Resources Officer (CHRO), the Director People and Culture Strategy provides enterprise leadership for People and Culture strategy, transformation and modernization, with responsibility for advancing the People Strategic Plan, divisional priorities, enterprise metrics and executive reporting, HR digital enablement, responsible AI adoption, diversity, inclusion and accessibility (DI&A), inclusive leadership and high-performing team leadership.

This role translates enterprise and divisional priorities into practical strategies, roadmaps, implementation plans, performance measures and governance mechanisms that strengthen organizational readiness, workforce planning, evidence-based decision-making and measurable impact across AGCO.

The ideal candidate is a trusted strategic advisor who brings strong judgment, systems thinking and a collaborative leadership style. They are comfortable operating in a complex public-sector environment, balancing long-term transformation with immediate operational priorities, and translating data, risk, workforce trends and stakeholder needs into practical, inclusive and measurable people strategies.

If you are motivated by the opportunity to lead strategic HR transformation, advance responsible digital and AI adoption, strengthen diversity, inclusion and accessibility, and support a strong employee experience, this role offers a meaningful platform to make a lasting enterprise-wide contribution at AGCO.

What You Will Do

Lead the development, implementation and ongoing refresh of AGCO’s People Strategic Plan, ensuring alignment with enterprise priorities, government mandates, workforce risks and evolving organizational needs.
Translate organizational priorities into actionable people strategies, roadmaps, initiatives, performance measures and implementation plans.
Oversee the planning, prioritization and delivery of People and Culture initiatives, projects and divisional priorities that advance organizational goals.
Establish planning, governance, reporting and accountability mechanisms to monitor progress against strategic commitments and demonstrate measurable impact.
Provide strategic advice to the CHRO, C-Suite, senior leaders and governance committees on HR priorities, workforce implications, transformation risks and organizational readiness.
Design and oversee enterprise People and Culture performance indicators, dashboards, workforce analytics and executive reporting to support transparency, accountability and evidence-informed decision-making.
Lead HR digital enablement and responsible AI adoption by developing practical capability, governance practices and high-value use cases that improve service quality, efficiency and decision-making.
Provide enterprise leadership for DI&A strategy, accessibility and inclusive leadership, embedding inclusion principles into AGCO culture, operations and people practices.
Lead the refresh, implementation and evaluation of enterprise DI&A strategy, including the development and reporting of meaningful performance measures.
Act as a senior subject matter expert on DI&A and accessibility, advising executives and senior leaders on inclusive talent practices, cultural transformation and emerging obligations.
Provide leadership and direction to a team by setting clear expectations, prioritizing deliverables, supporting development and fostering a culture of inclusion, accountability, learning and high

You Have

Post-secondary education in Human Resources, Organizational Development, Organizational Psychology, Adult Education, Strategic Planning, Leadership, Human Rights, Public Policy or a related field, or equivalent work experience; a master’s degree is considered an asset.
Minimum of 8 years progressive leadership experience in strategic planning, organizational transformation, HR strategy, performance measurement, workforce analytics, DI&A, accessibility, digital enablement and/or related areas.
Demonstrated ability to translate enterprise priorities into practical strategies, roadmaps, governance structures, implementation plans and measurable outcomes.
Strong understanding of HR digital adoption, HRIS-enabled process improvement, workflow automation, workforce analytics, digital service delivery, change management and responsible AI use.
Knowledge of HR data governance, privacy, accessibility, security, records management and ethical use of workforce information.
Experience developing executive-level reports, dashboards, briefings and presentations that translate complex information into clear insights and recommendations.
Strong consultation, facilitation, public speaking and stakeholder engagement skills, with the ability to influence and build alignment across senior leaders, governance bodies and cross-functional partners.
Demonstrated experience leading DI&A strategy, accessibility initiatives, inclusive leadership development, employee engagement forums, committees or enterprise-wide measurement frameworks.
Strong knowledge of Ontario legal and regulatory frameworks related to human rights, accessibility, employment standards and inclusive workplace practices.
Experience leading, coaching and developing teams in a complex, unionized and public-sector environment is an asset.
Eligibility to work in Canada and the ability to successfully complete a criminal background check.

To apply to this vacancy, please submit your application online at our Careers webpage located at Careers | Alcohol and Gaming Commission of Ontario. Please note that only applications submitted through the Applicant Tracking System will be accepted.

About The AGCO

The Alcohol and Gaming Commission of Ontario (AGCO) is an Ontario provincial regulatory agency that reports to the Ministry of the Attorney General. We are responsible for regulating the alcohol, gaming, horse racing and cannabis retail sectors in accordance with the principles of honesty and integrity, and in the public interest.

The AGCO is proud to be recognized as one of Greater Toronto’s Top Employers for the second year in a row. This annual distinction reflects our commitment to cultivating a workplace environment that prioritizes employee well-being, emphasizing work-life balance, mental health resources, and opportunities for professional growth. We remain committed to fostering a supportive and rewarding work environment for our employees.

What We Offer

The AGCO provides a comprehensive range of benefits and programs (subject to eligibility), including:

Generous time-off policy, including 2 volunteer days to contribute to causes that matter to you.
Defined benefit pension plans to secure your financial future.
Comprehensive health, dental, and vision plans, with 100% employer-paid premiums.
Well-being credits to support gym memberships, therapy, financial planning, and more.
Employer-paid parental leave top-up.
Professional development opportunities with access to training programs, leadership resources, and reimbursement for professional memberships.
24/7 confidential support through our Employee Assistance Program.
Convenient, central location near the subway line for easy access when working in the office. Paid onsite parking is also available.

Please note that only applications submitted through the Applicant Tracking System will be accepted.

The AGCO is an inclusive and equal opportunity employer.

The AGCO has the responsibility to lead by example in advancing racial equity and to build a diverse, inclusive, accessible and respectful workplace where every employee has a voice and the opportunity to fully contribute. To this effect, you are encouraged to reflect upon the diversity you would bring to the role within your application including, but not limited to, individuals identifying with one or more of the under-represented groups identified within Ontario’s Human Rights Code. 

Disability related accommodation during the recruitment process is available upon request. Persons with disabilities who require accommodation during the application process, or who need job postings in an alternative format, may email their request to askhr@agco.ca. The subject line should read “Accommodation in Application – [Position Title].

We do not use artificial intelligence (AI) tools to screen, assess, or select applicants at any stage of the hiring process. All applications will be reviewed and evaluated by our Human Resources team and hiring managers.

jobs.title: Deputy Chief Financial Officer
jobs.description:
Deputy Chief Financial Officer

Prince Rupert, BC
Reference # AC - 7380

Meridia Recruitment Solutions has partnered with the Prince Rupert Port Authority (PRPA) to recruit a Deputy Chief Financial Officer (Deputy CFO) to join their leadership team.

Reporting to the Chief Financial Officer, the Deputy CFO will provide leadership across accounting, treasury, financial planning and analysis, procurement, financial reporting, and capital finance. This role will play a key part in supporting strategic decision-making, overseeing day-to-day financial operations, and ensuring the organization maintains strong financial management, governance, and reporting practices.

YOUR RESPONSIBILITIES:

• Lead the annual budgeting, forecasting, and financial planning processes in support of organizational priorities and capital investment plans.
• Prepare financial analysis, business cases, and investment models to support executive and Board decision-making.
• Oversee treasury operations, liquidity management, financing arrangements, and banking relationships.
• Provide financial oversight of capital projects and procurement activities, ensuring effective budgeting, forecasting, and financial controls.
• Lead the preparation of accurate and timely IFRS-compliant financial statements and management reporting.
• Drive continuous improvement initiatives related to financial systems, reporting processes, internal controls, and finance operations.
• Coordinate the annual external audit process and ensure compliance with regulatory, taxation, and reporting requirements.
• Prepare materials and reporting for the Executive Leadership Team, Audit Committee, and Board of Directors.
• Partner with leaders across the organization to support budgeting, resource allocation, and operational decision-making.
• Lead, mentor, and develop a high-performing finance team while fostering a culture of accountability and continuous improvement.

YOUR REQUIREMENTS:

EDUCATION & EXPERIENCE

• Bachelor's degree in Finance, Accounting, Business Administration, or a related discipline.
• CPA designation required; MBA or other advanced business or finance education considered an asset.
• 10+ years of progressive finance leadership experience, including 5 years of experience in a senior finance role with responsibility for financial planning, reporting, treasury, and governance.
• Experience supporting Boards of Directors, Audit Committees, and senior executive leadership teams.

KEY SKILLS & CHARACTERISTICS

• Strong knowledge of IFRS, financial reporting, treasury management, internal controls, and financial planning practices.
• Demonstrated success improving finance functions, systems, processes, and reporting capabilities.
• Strong leadership, communication, and relationship-building skills.
• Experience within infrastructure, transportation, marine, logistics, public sector, or other capital-intensive industries would be considered an asset.
• Ability to obtain and maintain Transport Canada Security Clearance.

This is a current vacancy; salary range is $189,000 - $245,000.

To express interest in this opportunity, please click on the "Apply Now" button below.

For more information, please contact Adam Creaghan, Partner, at acreaghan@kbrs.ca or 647-336-1416 or Lauren MacDonald, Recruitment Specialist, at laurenmacdonald@kbrs.ca or 902-407-1427. If you require accommodation to participate in the recruitment process, please let Lauren know.

Meridia Recruitment Solutions connects leading organizations with top talent by building strong relationships and creating ideal matches with candidates because we are only successful when you are.

We appreciate your interest in this opportunity. To learn more about Meridia Recruitment Solutions, our job opportunities, and career advice, we invite you to explore our site and subscribe for career alerts.
